paper.title: Is the Risk of Bankruptcy a Systematic Risk?
paper.citation: Dichev, Ilia D. (1998), "Is the Risk of Bankruptcy a Systematic Risk?" The Journal of Finance 53(3), 1131-1147.

definition.value: Altman's (1968) Z-model bankruptcy score, where higher values indicate lower probability of bankruptcy.

economic_intuition.value: The score is an ex ante measure of bankruptcy risk used to test whether bankruptcy risk is systematic and priced in subsequent stock returns.

evidence.location: Section I, Research Design, Sample Selection, and Empirical Tests
evidence.quote: The result is a single composite bankruptcy score that reflects the ex ante probability of bankruptcy for each firm at a given point in time.

evidence.location: Section I, Research Design, Sample Selection, and Empirical Tests
evidence.quote: This study provides evidence on this question by investigating the empirical relation between risk of bankruptcy and systematic risk.

evidence.quote: Z is from Altman (1968), where higher Zs signify lower probability of bankruptcy.
evidence.interpretation: A higher Z score denotes greater financial strength and lower bankruptcy risk.
